blocks.text: REQUIRED PEDIATRIC ASSESSMENTS
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Under the Pediatric Research Equity Act (PREA) (21 U.S.C. 355c), all applications for new active ingredients, new indications, new dosage forms, new dosing regimens, or new routes of administration are required to contain an assessment of the safety and effectiveness of the product for the claimed indication in pediatric patients unless this requirement is waived, deferred, or inapplicable.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: We are waiving the pediatric study requirement for this application because necessary studies are impossible or highly impracticable as the disease does not exist in pediatric patients.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: RISK EVALUATION AND MITIGATION STRATEGY REQUIREMENTS
section_path: RISK EVALUATION AND MITIGATION STRATEGY REQUIREMENTS
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The REMS for Stelara (ustekinumab) was originally approved on September 25, 2009, and a REMS modification was approved on May 2, 2012. The REMS consists of a communication plan and a timetable for submission of assessments of the REMS. Your proposed modification to the REMS consists of a revised communication plan to include information about a new indication of Psoriatic Arthritis.
section_path: RISK EVALUATION AND MITIGATION STRATEGY REQUIREMENTS
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The timetable for submission of assessments of the REMS will remain the same as that approved on September 25, 2009.
section_path: RISK EVALUATION AND MITIGATION STRATEGY REQUIREMENTS
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: page_footer
blocks.text: Reference ID: 3376979
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The assessment plan has been revised to include evaluation of rheumatologists' understanding of the risks of Stelara (ustekinumab). The revised REMS assessment plan should include, but is not limited to, the following:
section_path: RISK EVALUATION AND MITIGATION STRATEGY REQUIREMENTS
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Evaluations of dermatologists and rheumatologists understanding of the risks of Stelara (ustekinumab), including evaluations of the following:
section_path: RISK EVALUATION AND MITIGATION STRATEGY REQUIREMENTS
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Prescribers' understanding of the risks of Stelara (ustekinumab) including the risks of serious infection, RPLS, and malignancy and how to select patients who are appropriate for treatment.
section_path: RISK EVALUATION AND MITIGATION STRATEGY REQUIREMENTS
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: A summary of all reported serious infections, RPLS, and malignancies with analysis of adverse event reporting by prescriber type (e.g., dermatologist, nurse, internist, oncologist), when available.
section_path: RISK EVALUATION AND MITIGATION STRATEGY REQUIREMENTS
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Based on the information submitted, an assessment and conclusion of whether the REMS is meeting its goals, and whether modifications to the REMS are needed.
section_path: RISK EVALUATION AND MITIGATION STRATEGY REQUIREMENTS
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The requirements for assessments of an approved REMS under section 505-1(g)(3) include with respect to each goal included in the strategy, an assessment of the extent to which the approved strategy, including each element of the strategy, is meeting the goal or whether 1 or more such goals or such elements should be modified.
section_path: RISK EVALUATION AND MITIGATION STRATEGY REQUIREMENTS
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: In addition to the assessments submitted according to the timetable included in the approved REMS, you must submit a REMS assessment and may propose a modification to the approved REMS when you submit a supplemental application for a new indication for use as described in section 505-1(g)(2)(A) of the FDCA.
section_path: RISK EVALUATION AND MITIGATION STRATEGY REQUIREMENTS

blocks.text: STELARA ® (ustekinumab) injection, for subcutaneous use Initial U.S. Approval: 2009
blocks.speaker: regulator

cells.text: Warnings and Precautions, Reversible Posterior Leukoencephalopathy

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: STELARA ® is a human interleukin-12 and -23 antagonist indicated for the treatment of adult patients (18 years or older) with
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  moderate to severe plaque psoriasis (Ps) who are candidates for phototherapy or systemic therapy. (1.1)
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  active psoriatic arthritis (PsA), alone or in combination with methotrexate. (1.2)
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: STELARA ® is administered by subcutaneous injection. (2)
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Psoriasis
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  For patients weighing <100 kg (220 lbs), the recommended dose is 45 mg initially and 4 weeks later, followed by 45 mg every 12 weeks. (2.1)
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  For patients weighing >100 kg (220 lbs), the recommended dose is 90 mg initially and 4 weeks later, followed by 90 mg every 12 weeks. (2.1)
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Psoriatic Arthritis
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  The recommended dose is 45 mg initially and 4 weeks later, followed by 45 mg every 12 weeks. (2.1).
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  For patients with co-existent moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis weighing >100 kg (220 lbs), the recommended dose is 90 mg initially and 4 weeks later, followed by 90 mg every 12 weeks. (2.1)
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Injection: 45 mg/0.5 mL in a single-use prefilled syringe (3)
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Injection: 90 mg/mL in a single-use prefilled syringe (3)
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Injection: 45 mg/0.5 mL in a single-use vial (3)
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Injection: 90 mg/mL in a single-use vial (3)
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Clinically significant hypersensitivity to ustekinumab or to any of the excipients. (4)
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Infections: Serious infections have occurred. Do not start STELARA ® during any clinically important active infection. If a serious infection develops, stop STELARA ® until the infection resolves. (5.1)
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Theoretical Risk for Particular Infections: Serious infections from mycobacteria, salmonella and Bacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG) vaccinations have been reported in patients genetically deficient in IL12/IL-23. Diagnostic tests for these infections should be considered as dictated by clinical circumstances. (5.2)
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Tuberculosis (TB): Evaluate patients for TB prior to initiating treatment with STELARA ® . Initiate treatment of latent TB before administering STELARA ® . (5.3)
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Malignancies: STELARA ® may increase risk of malignancy. The safety of STELARA ® in patients with a history of or a known malignancy has not been evaluated. (5.4)
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Anaphylaxis or other clinically significant hypersensitivity reactions may occur. (5.5)
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Reversible Posterior Leukoencephalopathy Syndrome (RPLS): One case was reported. If suspected, treat promptly and discontinue STELARA ® . (5.6)
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥3% and greater than with placebo): Nasopharyngitis, upper respiratory tract infection, headache, and fatigue. (6.1)
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: To report SUSPECTED ADVERSE REACTIONS, contact Janssen Biotech, Inc. at 1-800-JANSSEN (1-800-526-7736) or FDA at 1800-FDA-1088 or www.fda.gov/medwatch.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Live vaccines: Live vaccines should not be given with STELARA ® . (7.1)
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Concomitant therapy: In psoriasis studies, the safety of concomitant use of STELARA ® with immunosuppressants or phototherapy has not been evaluated. (7.2)
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 1 INDICATIONS AND USAGE
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 1.1 Psoriasis (Ps)
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: STELARA ® is indicated for the treatment of adult patients (18 years or older) with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis who are candidates for phototherapy or systemic therapy.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 1.2 Psoriatic Arthritis (PsA)
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: STELARA ® is indicated for the treatment of adult patients (18 years or older) with active psoriatic arthritis. STELARA ® can be used alone or in combination with methotrexate (MTX).
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 2 DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 2.1 Dosing
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: STELARA ® is administered by subcutaneous injection.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Psoriasis
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  For patients weighing <100 kg (220 lbs), the recommended dose is 45 mg initially and 4 weeks later, followed by 45 mg every 12 weeks.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  For patients weighing >100 kg (220 lbs), the recommended dose is 90 mg initially and 4 weeks later, followed by 90 mg every 12 weeks.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: In subjects weighing >100 kg, 45 mg was also shown to be efficacious. However, 90 mg resulted in greater efficacy in these subjects [see Clinical Studies (14)].
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Psoriatic Arthritis
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  The recommended dose is 45 mg initially and 4 weeks later, followed by 45 mg every 12 weeks.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  For patients with co-existent moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis weighing >100 kg (220 lbs), the recommended dose is 90 mg initially and 4 weeks later, followed by 90 mg every 12 weeks.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 2.2 General Considerations for Administration
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: STELARA ® is for subcutaneous administration. STELARA ® is intended for use under the guidance and supervision of a physician. STELARA ® should only be administered to patients who will be closely monitored and have regular follow-up visits with a physician.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: After proper training in subcutaneous injection technique, a patient may self inject with STELARA ® if a physician determines that it is appropriate. Patients should be instructed to follow the directions provided in the Medication Guide (see Medication Guide).
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: page_footer
blocks.text: Reference ID: 3376979
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Prior to administration, STELARA ® should be visually inspected for particulate matter and discoloration. STELARA ® is colorless to light yellow and may contain a few small translucent or white particles. STELARA ® should not be used if it is discolored or cloudy, or if other particulate matter is present. STELARA ® does not contain preservatives; therefore, any unused product remaining in the vial and/or syringe should be discarded.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The needle cover on the prefilled syringe contains dry natural rubber (a derivative of latex). The needle cover should not be handled by persons sensitive to latex.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: It is recommended that each injection be administered at a different anatomic location (such as upper arms, gluteal regions, thighs, or any quadrant of abdomen) than the previous injection, and not into areas where the skin is tender, bruised, erythematous, or indurated. When using the single-use vial, a 27 gauge, ½ inch needle is recommended.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 2.3 Instructions for Administration of STELARA ® Prefilled Syringes Equipped with Needle Safety Guard
section_path: 2.3 Instructions for Administration of STELARA ® Prefilled Syringes Equipped with Needle Safety Guard
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Refer to the diagram below for the provided instructions.
section_path: 2.3 Instructions for Administration of STELARA ® Prefilled Syringes Equipped with Needle Safety Guard
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: To prevent premature activation of the needle safety guard, do not touch the NEEDLE GUARD ACTIVATION CLIPS at any time during use.
section_path: 2.3 Instructions for Administration of STELARA ® Prefilled Syringes Equipped with Needle Safety Guard
blocks.speaker: regulator

section_path: 2.3 Instructions for Administration of STELARA ® Prefilled Syringes Equipped with Needle Safety Guard
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Hold the BODY and remove the NEEDLE COVER. Do not hold the PLUNGER or PLUNGER HEAD while removing the NEEDLE COVER or the PLUNGER may move. Do not use the prefilled syringe if it is dropped without the NEEDLE COVER in place.
section_path: 2.3 Instructions for Administration of STELARA ® Prefilled Syringes Equipped with Needle Safety Guard
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Inject STELARA ® subcutaneously as recommended [see Dosage and Administration (2.2)].
section_path: 2.3 Instructions for Administration of STELARA ® Prefilled Syringes Equipped with Needle Safety Guard
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Inject all of the medication by pushing in the PLUNGER until the PLUNGER HEAD is completely between the needle guard wings. Injection of the entire prefilled syringe contents is necessary to activate the needle guard.
section_path: 2.3 Instructions for Administration of STELARA ® Prefilled Syringes Equipped with Needle Safety Guard
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: page_footer
blocks.text: Reference ID: 3376979
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  After injection, maintain the pressure on the PLUNGER HEAD and remove the needle from the skin. Slowly take your thumb off the PLUNGER HEAD to allow the empty syringe to move up until the entire needle is covered by the needle guard, as shown by the illustration below:
section_path: 2.3 Instructions for Administration of STELARA ® Prefilled Syringes Equipped with Needle Safety Guard
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Used syringes should be placed in a puncture-resistant container.

blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 3 DOSAGE FORMS AND STRENGTHS
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: STELARA ® solution is colorless to slightly yellow in appearance and contains 90 mg ustekinumab per mL.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Injection: 45 mg/0.5 mL in a single-use prefilled syringe
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Injection: 90 mg/1 mL in a single-use prefilled syringe
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Injection: 45 mg/0.5 mL in a single-use vial
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Injection: 90 mg/1 mL in a single-use vial
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 4 CONTRAINDICATIONS
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Clinically significant hypersensitivity to ustekinumab or to any of the excipients [see Warnings and Precautions (5.5)].
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: page_footer
blocks.text: Reference ID: 3376979
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 5 WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 5.1 Infections
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: STELARA ® may increase the risk of infections and reactivation of latent infections. Serious bacterial, fungal, and viral infections were observed in subjects receiving STELARA ® [see Adverse Reactions (6.1)].
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: STELARA ® should not be given to patients with any clinically important active infection. STELARA ® should not be administered until the infection resolves or is adequately treated. Instruct patients to seek medical advice if signs or symptoms suggestive of an infection occur. Exercise caution when considering the use of STELARA ® in patients with a chronic infection or a history of recurrent infection.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Serious infections requiring hospitalization occurred in the psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis development programs. In the psoriasis program, serious infections included diverticulitis, cellulitis, pneumonia, appendicitis, cholecystitis and sepsis. In the psoriatic arthritis program, serious infections included cholecystitis.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 5.2 Theoretical Risk for Vulnerability to Particular Infections
section_path: 5.2 Theoretical Risk for Vulnerability to Particular Infections
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Individuals genetically deficient in IL-12/IL-23 are particularly vulnerable to disseminated infections from mycobacteria (including nontuberculous, environmental mycobacteria), salmonella (including nontyphi strains), and Bacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG) vaccinations. Serious infections and fatal outcomes have been reported in such patients.
section_path: 5.2 Theoretical Risk for Vulnerability to Particular Infections
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: It is not known whether patients with pharmacologic blockade of IL-12/IL-23 from treatment with STELARA ® will be susceptible to these types of infections. Appropriate diagnostic testing should be considered, e.g., tissue culture, stool culture, as dictated by clinical circumstances.
section_path: 5.2 Theoretical Risk for Vulnerability to Particular Infections
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 5.3 Pre-treatment Evaluation for Tuberculosis
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Evaluate patients for tuberculosis infection prior to initiating treatment with STELARA ® .
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Do not administer STELARA ® to patients with active tuberculosis. Initiate treatment of latent tuberculosis prior to administering STELARA ® . Consider anti-tuberculosis therapy prior to initiation of STELARA ® in patients with a past history of latent or active tuberculosis in whom an adequate course of treatment cannot be confirmed. Patients receiving STELARA ® should be monitored closely for signs and symptoms of active tuberculosis during and after treatment.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 5.4 Malignancies
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: STELARA ® is an immunosuppressant and may increase the risk of malignancy. Malignancies were reported among subjects who received STELARA ® in clinical studies [see Adverse Reactions (6.1)]. In rodent models, inhibition of IL-12/IL-23p40 increased the risk of malignancy [see Nonclinical Toxicology (13)].
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: page_footer
blocks.text: Reference ID: 3376979
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The safety of STELARA ® has not been evaluated in patients who have a history of malignancy or who have a known malignancy.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: There have been post marketing reports of the rapid appearance of multiple cutaneous squamous cell carcinomas in patients receiving STELARA ® who had pre-existing risk factors for developing non-melanoma skin cancer. All patients receiving STELARA ® should be monitored for the appearance of non-melanoma skin cancer. Patients greater than 60 years of age, those with a medical history of prolonged immunosuppressant therapy and those with a history of PUVA treatment should be followed closely [see Adverse Reactions (6.1)].
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 5.5 Hypersensitivity Reactions
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis and angioedema, have been reported postmarketing. If an anaphylactic or other clinically significant hypersensitivity reaction occurs, institute appropriate therapy and discontinue STELARA ® [see Adverse Reactions (6.3)].
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 5.6 Reversible Posterior Leukoencephalopathy Syndrome
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: One case of reversible posterior leukoencephalopathy syndrome (RPLS) was observed during the psoriasis clinical development program which included 3758 STELARA ® -treated subjects. The subject, who had received 12 doses of STELARA ® over approximately two years, presented with headache, seizures and confusion. No additional STELARA ® injections were administered and the subject fully recovered with appropriate treatment. No additional cases of RPLS were observed in the psoriatic arthritis clinical development program which included 914 STELARA ® -treated subjects.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: RPLS is a neurological disorder, which is not caused by demyelination or a known infectious agent. RPLS can present with headache, seizures, confusion and visual disturbances. Conditions with which it has been associated include preeclampsia, eclampsia, acute hypertension, cytotoxic agents and immunosuppressive therapy. Fatal outcomes have been reported.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: If RPLS is suspected, administer appropriate treatment and discontinue STELARA ® .
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 5.7 Immunizations
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Prior to initiating therapy with STELARA ® , patients should receive all immunizations appropriate for age as recommended by current immunization guidelines. Patients being treated with STELARA ® should not receive live vaccines. BCG vaccines should not be given during treatment with STELARA ® or for one year prior to initiating treatment or one year following discontinuation of treatment. Caution is advised when administering live vaccines to household contacts of patients receiving STELARA ® because of the potential risk for shedding from the household contact and transmission to patient.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Non-live vaccinations received during a course of STELARA ® may not elicit an immune response sufficient to prevent disease.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: page_footer
blocks.text: Reference ID: 3376979
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 5.8 Concomitant Therapies
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: In psoriasis studies the safety of STELARA ® in combination with immunosuppressive agents or phototherapy has not been evaluated. In psoriatic arthritis studies, concomitant MTX use did not appear to influence the safety or efficacy of STELARA ® [see Drug Interactions (7.2)]. Ultraviolet-induced skin cancers developed earlier and more frequently in mice genetically manipulated to be deficient in both IL-12 and IL-23 or IL-12 alone [see Nonclinical Toxicology (13)].
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 6 ADVERSE REACTIONS
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 6.1 Clinical Studies Experience
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Because clinical trials are conducted under widely varying conditions, adverse reaction rates observed in the clinical trials of a drug cannot be directly compared to rates in the clinical trials of another drug and may not reflect the rates observed in practice.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Psoriasis Clinical Studies
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The safety data reflect exposure to STELARA ® in 3117 psoriasis subjects, including 2414 exposed for at least 6 months, 1855 exposed for at least one year, 1653 exposed for at least two years, 1569 exposed for at least three years, 1482 exposed for at least four years and 838 exposed for at least five years.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Table 1 summarizes the adverse reactions that occurred at a rate of at least 1% and at a higher rate in the STELARA ® groups than the placebo group during the placebo-controlled period of Ps STUDY 1 and Ps STUDY 2 [see Clinical Studies (14)].
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: caption
blocks.text: Table 1. Adverse reactions reported by ≥1% of subjects through Week 12 in Ps STUDY 1 and Ps STUDY 2
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: STELARA ®
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: page_footer
blocks.text: Reference ID: 3376979
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Adverse reactions that occurred at rates less than 1% in the controlled period of Ps STUDIES 1 and 2 through week 12 included: cellulitis, herpes zoster, diverticulitis and certain injection site reactions (pain, swelling, pruritus, induration, hemorrhage, bruising, and irritation).
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: One case of RPLS occurred during clinical trials [see Warnings and Precautions (5.6)].
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Infections
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: In the placebo-controlled period of clinical studies of psoriasis subjects (average follow-up of 12.6 weeks for placebo-treated subjects and 13.4 weeks for STELARA ® -treated subjects), 27% of STELARA ® -treated subjects reported infections (1.39 per subject-year of follow-up) compared with 24% of placebo-treated subjects (1.21 per subject-year of follow-up). Serious infections occurred in 0.3% of STELARA ® -treated subjects (0.01 per subject-year of follow-up) and in 0.4% of placebo-treated subjects (0.02 per subject-year of follow-up) [see Warnings and Precautions (5.1)].
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: In the controlled and non-controlled portions of psoriasis clinical trials (median follow up of 3.2 years), representing 8998 subject-years of exposure, 72.3% of STELARA ® -treated subjects reported infections (0.87 per subject-years of follow-up). Serious infections were reported in 2.8% of subjects (0.01 per subject-years of follow-up).
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Malignancies
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: In the controlled and non-controlled portions of psoriasis clinical trials (median follow up of 3.2 years, representing 8998 subject-years of exposure), 1.7% of STELARA ® -treated subjects reported malignancies excluding non-melanoma skin cancers (0.60 per hundred subject-years of follow-up). Non-melanoma skin cancer was reported in 1.5% of STELARA ® -treated subjects (0.52 per hundred subject-years of follow-up) [see Warnings and Precautions (5.4)]. The most frequently observed malignancies other than non-melanoma skin cancer during the clinical trials were: prostate, melanoma, colorectal and breast. Malignancies other than non-melanoma skin cancer in STELARA ® -treated patients during the controlled and uncontrolled portions of studies were similar in type and number to what would be expected in the general U.S. population according to the SEER database (adjusted for age, gender and race). 1
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Psoriatic Arthritis Clinical Studies
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The safety of STELARA ® was assessed in 927 patients in two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled studies in adult patients with active psoriatic arthritis (PsA). The overall safety profile of STELARA ® in patients with PsA was consistent with the safety profile seen in psoriasis clinical studies. A higher incidence of arthralgia, nausea, and dental infections was observed in STELARA ® -treated patients when compared with placebo-treated patients (3% vs. 1% for arthralgia and 3% vs. 1% for nausea; 1% vs. 0.6% for dental infections) in the placebocontrolled portions of the PsA clinical trials.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: page_footer
blocks.text: Reference ID: 3376979
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 6.2 Immunogenicity
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Approximately 6% of patients treated with STELARA ® in psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis clinical studies developed antibodies to ustekinumab, which were generally low-titer. No apparent association between the development of antibodies to ustekinumab and the development of injection site reactions was seen. No ustekinumab-related serious hypersensitivity reactions were observed in psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis clinical trials. In psoriasis studies, the majority of patients who were positive for antibodies to ustekinumab had neutralizing antibodies.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The data above reflect the percentage of subjects whose test results were positive for antibodies to ustekinumab and are highly dependent on the sensitivity and specificity of the assay. Additionally, the observed incidence of antibody positivity in an assay may be influenced by several factors, including sample handling, timing of sample collection, concomitant medications and underlying disease. For these reasons, comparison of the incidence of antibodies to ustekinumab with the incidence of antibodies to other products may be misleading.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 6.3 Post-marketing Experience
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Adverse reactions have been reported during post-approval use with STELARA ® . Because these reactions are reported voluntarily from a population of uncertain size, it is not always possible to reliably estimate their frequency or establish a causal relationship to STELARA ® exposure.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Immune system disorders: Serious hypersensitivity reactions (including anaphylaxis and angioedema), other hypersensitivity reactions (including rash and urticaria).
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Skin reactions: Pustular psoriasis, erythrodermic psoriasis.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 7 DRUG INTERACTIONS
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Drug interaction studies have not been conducted with STELARA ® .
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 7.1 Live Vaccines
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Live vaccines should not be given concurrently with STELARA ® [see Warnings and Precautions (5.7)].
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 7.2 Concomitant Therapies
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: In psoriasis studies the safety of STELARA ® in combination with immunosuppressive agents or phototherapy has not been evaluated. In psoriatic arthritis studies, concomitant MTX use did not appear to influence the safety or efficacy of STELARA ® [see Warnings and Precautions (5.8)].
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 7.3 CYP450 Substrates
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The formation of CYP450 enzymes can be altered by increased levels of certain cytokines (e.g., IL-1, IL-6, IL-10, TNFα, IFN) during chronic inflammation. Thus, STELARA ® , an antagonist of IL-12 and IL-23, could normalize the formation of CYP450 enzymes. Upon initiation of STELARA ® in patients who are receiving concomitant CYP450 substrates, particularly those with a narrow therapeutic index, monitoring for therapeutic effect (e.g., for warfarin) or drug concentration (e.g., for cyclosporine) should be considered and the individual dose of the drug adjusted as needed [see Clinical Pharmacology (12.3)].
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: page_footer
blocks.text: Reference ID: 3376979
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 7.4 Allergen Immunotherapy
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: STELARA ® has not been evaluated in patients who have undergone allergy immunotherapy. STELARA ® may decrease the protective effect of allergen immunotherapy (decrease tolerance) which may increase the risk of an allergic reaction to a dose of allergen immunotherapy. Therefore, caution should be exercised in patients receiving or who have received allergen immunotherapy, particularly for anaphylaxis.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 8 USE IN SPECIFIC POPULATIONS
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 8.1 Pregnancy
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Pregnancy Category B
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: There are no adequate and well controlled studies of STELARA ® in pregnant women. Developmental toxicity studies conducted with monkeys found no evidence of harm to the fetus due to ustekinumab. STELARA ® should be used during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Ustekinumab was tested in two embryo-fetal development toxicity studies with cynomologus monkeys. No teratogenic effects or other adverse developmental effects were observed in fetuses from pregnant monkeys that were administered ustekinumab during the period of organogenesis either twice weekly via subcutaneous injections or weekly by intravenous injections at doses up to 45 times the maximum recommended human dose (MRHD) (on a mg/kg basis at a maternal dose of 45 mg/kg).
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: In a combined embryo-fetal development and pre- and post-natal development toxicity study, pregnant cynomolgus monkeys were administered subcutaneous doses of ustekinumab twice weekly up to 45 times the MRHD (on a mg/kg basis at a maternal dose of 45 mg/kg) from the beginning of organogenesis to Day 33 after delivery. Neonatal deaths occurred in the offspring of one monkey administered ustekinumab at 22.5 mg/kg and one monkey dosed at 45 mg/kg. No ustekinumab-related effects on functional, morphological, or immunological development were observed in the neonates from birth through six months of age.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 8.3 Nursing Mothers
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Caution should be exercised when STELARA ® is administered to a nursing woman. The unknown risks to the infant from gastrointestinal or systemic exposure to ustekinumab should be weighed against the known benefits of breast-feeding. Ustekinumab is excreted in the milk of lactating monkeys administered ustekinumab. IgG is excreted in human milk, so it is expected that STELARA ® will be present in human milk. It is not known if ustekinumab is absorbed systemically after ingestion; however, published data suggest that antibodies in breast milk do not enter the neonatal and infant circulation in substantial amounts.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: page_footer
blocks.text: Reference ID: 3376979
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 8.4 Pediatric Use
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Safety and effectiveness of STELARA ® in pediatric patients have not been evaluated.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 8.5 Geriatric Use
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Of the 4031 subjects exposed to STELARA ® , a total of 248 were 65 years or older (183 patients with psoriasis and 65 patients with psoriatic arthritis), and 29 subjects were 75 years or older. Although no differences in safety or efficacy were observed between older and younger subjects, the number of subjects aged 65 and over is not sufficient to determine whether they respond differently from younger subjects.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 10 OVERDOSAGE
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Single doses up to 6 mg/kg intravenously have been administered in clinical studies without dose-limiting toxicity. In case of overdosage, it is recommended that the patient be monitored for any signs or symptoms of adverse reactions or effects and appropriate symptomatic treatment be instituted immediately.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 11 DESCRIPTION
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: STELARA ® is a human IgG1κ monoclonal antibody against the p40 subunit of the IL-12 and IL23 cytokines. Using DNA recombinant technology, STELARA ® is produced in a well characterized recombinant cell line and is purified using standard bio-processing technology. The manufacturing process contains steps for the clearance of viruses. STELARA ® is comprised of 1326 amino acids and has an estimated molecular mass that ranges from 148,079 to 149,690 Daltons.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: STELARA ® , for subcutaneous use, is available as: 45 mg of ustekinumab in 0.5 mL and 90 mg of ustekinumab in 1 mL. STELARA ® is supplied as a sterile solution in a single-use prefilled syringe with a 27 gauge fixed ½ inch needle, or a single-use 2 mL Type I glass vial with a coated stopper. The syringe is fitted with a passive needle guard and a needle cover that is manufactured using a dry natural rubber (a derivative of latex).
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Each 45 mg ustekinumab prefilled syringe also contains: L-histidine and L-histidine monohydrochloride monohydrate (0.5 mg), Polysorbate 80 (0.02 mg), and sucrose (38 mg) to fill to a final volume of 0.5 mL.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Each 90 mg ustekinumab prefilled syringe also contains: L-histidine and L-histidine monohydrochloride monohydrate (1 mg), Polysorbate 80 (0.04 mg), and sucrose (76 mg) to fill to a final volume of 1 mL.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: page_footer
blocks.text: Reference ID: 3376979
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Each 45 mg ustekinumab vial also contains: L-histidine and L-histidine monohydrochloride monohydrate (0.5 mg), Polysorbate 80 (0.02 mg), and sucrose (38 mg) to fill to a final volume of 0.5 mL.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Each 90 mg ustekinumab vial also contains: L-histidine and L-histidine monohydrochloride monohydrate (1 mg), Polysorbate 80 (0.04 mg), and sucrose (76 mg) to fill to a final volume of 1 mL.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The STELARA ® solution is colorless to slightly yellow in appearance and has a pH of 5.7-6.3. STELARA ® does not contain preservatives.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 12 CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 12.1 Mechanism of Action
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Ustekinumab is a human IgG1қ monoclonal antibody that binds with specificity to the shared p40 protein subunit used by both the IL-12 and IL-23 cytokines. IL-12 and IL-23 are naturally occurring cytokines that are involved in inflammatory and immune responses, such as natural killer cell activation and CD4+ T-cell differentiation and activation. Levels of IL-12/23 and p40 are elevated in the skin and blood of psoriasis patients, and blood of psoriatic arthritis patients implicating IL-12 and IL-23 in the pathophysiology of psoriatic inflammatory diseases. In in vitro models, ustekinumab was shown to disrupt IL-12 and IL-23 mediated signaling and cytokine cascades by disrupting the interaction of these cytokines with a shared cell-surface receptor chain, IL-12R1.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 12.2 Pharmacodynamics
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: In a small exploratory study, a decrease was observed in the expression of mRNA of its molecular targets IL-12 and IL-23 in lesional skin biopsies measured at baseline and up to two weeks post-treatment in subjects with psoriasis.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 12.3 Pharmacokinetics
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Absorption
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: In subjects with psoriasis, the median time to reach the maximum serum concentration (Tmax) was 13.5 days and 7 days, respectively, after a single subcutaneous administration of 45 mg (N=22) and 90 mg (N=24) of ustekinumab. In healthy subjects (N=30), the median Tmax value (8.5 days) following a single subcutaneous administration of 90 mg of ustekinumab was comparable to that observed in subjects with psoriasis. Following multiple subcutaneous doses of STELARA ® , the steady-state serum concentrations of ustekinumab were achieved by Week 28. The mean (±SD) steady-state trough serum concentration ranged from 0.31 ± 0.33 mcg/mL (45 mg) to 0.64 ± 0.64 mcg/mL (90 mg). There was no apparent accumulation in serum ustekinumab concentration over time when given subcutaneously every 12 weeks.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: page_footer
blocks.text: Reference ID: 3376979
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Distribution
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Following subcutaneous administration of 45 mg (N=18) and 90 mg (N=21) of ustekinumab to subjects with psoriasis, the mean (±SD) apparent volume of distribution during the terminal phase (Vz/F) was 161 ± 65 mL/kg and 179 ± 85 mL/kg, respectively. The mean (± SD) volume of distribution during the terminal phase (Vz) following a single intravenous administration to subjects with psoriasis ranged from 56.1 ± 6.5 to 82.1 ± 23.6 mL/kg.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Metabolism
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The metabolic pathway of ustekinumab has not been characterized. As a human IgG1 monoclonal antibody ustekinumab is expected to be degraded into small peptides and amino acids via catabolic pathways in the same manner as endogenous IgG.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Elimination
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The mean (± SD) systemic clearance (CL) following a single intravenous administration of ustekinumab to subjects with psoriasis ranged from 1.90 ± 0.28 to 2.22 ± 0.63 mL/day/kg. The mean (±SD) half-life ranged from 14.9 ± 4.6 to 45.6 ± 80.2 days across all psoriasis studies following intravenous and subcutaneous administration.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Weight
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: When given the same dose, subjects with psoriasis or psoriatic arthritis weighing >100 kg had lower median serum ustekinumab concentrations compared with those subjects weighing ≤100 kg. The median trough serum concentrations of ustekinumab in subjects of higher weight (>100 kg) in the 90 mg group were comparable to those in subjects of lower weight (≤100 kg) in the 45 mg group.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Hepatic and Renal Impairment
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: No pharmacokinetic data are available in patients with hepatic or renal impairment.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Elderly
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: A population pharmacokinetic analysis (N=106/1937 subjects greater than or equal to 65 years old) was performed to evaluate the effect of age on the pharmacokinetics of ustekinumab. There were no apparent changes in pharmacokinetic parameters (clearance and volume of distribution) in subjects older than 65 years old.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Drug-Drug Interactions
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The effects of IL-12 or IL-23 on the regulation of CYP450 enzymes were evaluated in an in vitro study using human hepatocytes, which showed that IL-12 and/or IL-23 at levels of 10 ng/mL did not alter human CYP450 enzyme activities (CYP1A2, 2B6, 2C9, 2C19, 2D6, or 3A4). However, the clinical relevance of in vitro data has not been established [see Drug Interactions (7.3)].
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Population pharmacokinetic data analyses indicated that the clearance of ustekinumab was not impacted by concomitant MTX, NSAIDs, and oral corticosteroids, or prior exposure to antiTNFα agents in patients with psoriatic arthritis.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: page_footer
blocks.text: Reference ID: 3376979
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 13 NONCLINICAL TOXICOLOGY
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 13.1 Carcinogenesis, Mutagenesis, Impairment of Fertility
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Animal studies have not been conducted to evaluate the carcinogenic or mutagenic potential of STELARA ® . Published literature showed that administration of murine IL-12 caused an antitumor effect in mice that contained transplanted tumors and IL-12/IL-23p40 knockout mice or mice treated with anti-IL-12/IL-23p40 antibody had decreased host defense to tumors. Mice genetically manipulated to be deficient in both IL-12 and IL-23 or IL-12 alone developed UVinduced skin cancers earlier and more frequently compared to wild-type mice. The relevance of these experimental findings in mouse models for malignancy risk in humans is unknown.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: No effects on fertility were observed in male cynomologus monkeys that were administered ustekinumab at subcutaneous doses up to 45 mg/kg twice weekly (45 times the MRHD on a mg/kg basis) prior to and during the mating period. However, fertility and pregnancy outcomes were not evaluated in mated females.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: No effects on fertility were observed in female mice that were administered an analogous IL12/IL-23p40 antibody by subcutaneous administration at doses up to 50 mg/kg, twice weekly, prior to and during early pregnancy.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 13.2 Animal Toxicology and/or Pharmacology
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: In a 26-week toxicology study, one out of 10 monkeys subcutaneously administered 45 mg/kg ustekinumab twice weekly for 26 weeks had a bacterial infection.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 14 CLINICAL STUDIES
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 14.1 Psoriasis
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Two multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled studies (Ps STUDY 1 and Ps STUDY 2) enrolled a total of 1996 subjects 18 years of age and older with plaque psoriasis who had a minimum body surface area involvement of 10%, and Psoriasis Area and Severity Index (PASI) score >12, and who were candidates for phototherapy or systemic therapy. Subjects with guttate, erythrodermic, or pustular psoriasis were excluded from the studies.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Ps STUDY 1 enrolled 766 subjects and Ps STUDY 2 enrolled 1230 subjects. The studies had the same design through Week 28. In both studies, subjects were randomized in equal proportion to placebo, 45 mg or 90 mg of STELARA ® . Subjects randomized to STELARA ® received 45 mg or 90 mg doses, regardless of weight, at Weeks 0, 4, and 16. Subjects randomized to receive placebo at Weeks 0 and 4 crossed over to receive STELARA ® (either 45 mg or 90 mg) at Weeks 12 and 16.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: In both studies, the endpoints were the proportion of subjects who achieved at least a 75% reduction in PASI score (PASI 75) from baseline to Week 12 and treatment success (cleared or minimal) on the Physician's Global Assessment (PGA). The PGA is a 6-category scale ranging from 0 (cleared) to 5 (severe) that indicates the physician's overall assessment of psoriasis focusing on plaque thickness/induration, erythema, and scaling.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: page_footer
blocks.text: Reference ID: 3376979
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: In both studies, subjects in all treatment groups had a median baseline PASI score ranging from approximately 17 to 18. Baseline PGA score was marked or severe in 44% of subjects in Ps STUDY 1 and 40% of subjects in Ps STUDY 2. Approximately two-thirds of all subjects had received prior phototherapy, 69% had received either prior conventional systemic or biologic therapy for the treatment of psoriasis, with 56% receiving prior conventional systemic therapy and 43% receiving prior biologic therapy. A total of 28% of study subjects had a history of psoriatic arthritis.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 14.2 Psoriatic Arthritis
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The safety and efficacy of STELARA ® was assessed in 927 patients (PsA STUDY 1, n=615; PsA STUDY 2, n=312), in two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled studies in adult patients 18 years of age and older with active PsA (5 swollen joints and ≥5 tender joints) despite non-steroidal anti-inflammatory (NSAID) or disease modifying antirheumatic (DMARD) therapy. Patients in these studies had a diagnosis of PsA for at least 6 months. Patients with each subtype of PsA were enrolled, including polyarticular arthritis with the absence of rheumatoid nodules (39%), spondylitis with peripheral arthritis (28%), asymmetric peripheral arthritis (21%), distal interphalangeal involvement (12%) and arthritis mutilans (0.5%). Over 70% and 40% of the patients, respectively, had enthesitis and dactylitis at baseline.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Patients were randomized to receive treatment with STELARA ® 45 mg, 90 mg, or placebo subcutaneously at Weeks 0 and 4 followed by every 12 weeks (q12w) dosing. Approximately 50% of patients continued on stable doses of MTX (≤25 mg/week). The primary endpoint was the percentage of patients achieving ACR 20 response at Week 24.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: In PsA STUDY 1 and PsA STUDY 2, 80% and 86% of the patients, respectively, had been previously treated with DMARDs. In PsA STUDY 1, previous treatment with anti-tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α agent was not allowed. In PsA STUDY 2, 58% (n=180) of the patients had been previously treated with an anti-TNFα agent, of whom over 70% had discontinued their anti-TNFα treatment for lack of efficacy or intolerance at any time.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Clinical Response
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.text: In both studies, a greater proportion of patients achieved ACR 20, ACR 50 and PASI 75 response in the STELARA ® 45 mg and 90 mg groups compared to placebo at Week 24 (see Table 4). ACR 70 responses were also higher in the STELARA ® 45 mg and 90 mg groups, although the difference was only numerical (p=NS) m Study 2. Responses were similar m patients regardless of prior TNFa exposure.

blocks.text: 16 HOW SUPPLIED/STORAGE AND HANDLING
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: STELARA ® does not contain preservatives. STELARA ® is available in single-use prefilled syringes or single-use vials containing 45 mg or 90 mg of ustekinumab. Each prefilled syringe is equipped with a needle safety guard.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The NDC number for the 45 mg prefilled syringe is 57894-060-03.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.text: The NDC number for the 90 mg prefilled syringe is 57894-061-03.

blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text

blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Storage and Stability
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: STELARA ® vials and prefilled syringes must be refrigerated at 2ºC to 8ºC (36ºF to 46ºF). Store STELARA ® vials upright. Keep the product in the original carton to protect from light until the time of use. Do not freeze. Do not shake. STELARA ® does not contain a preservative; discard any unused portion.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 17 PATIENT COUNSELING INFORMATION
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: See FDA-approved patient labeling (Medication Guide and Instructions for Use)
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Instruct patients to read the Medication Guide before starting STELARA ® therapy and to reread the Medication Guide each time the prescription is renewed.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Infections
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Inform patients that STELARA ® may lower the ability of their immune system to fight infections. Instruct patients of the importance of communicating any history of infections to the doctor, and contacting their doctor if they develop any symptoms of infection.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Malignancies
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Patients should be counseled about the risk of malignancies while receiving STELARA ® .
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Allergic Reactions
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Advise patients to seek immediate medical attention if they experience any symptoms of serious allergic reactions.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 17.1 Instruction on Injection Technique
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The first self-injection should be performed under the supervision of a qualified healthcare professional. If a patient or caregiver is to administer STELARA ® , he/she should be instructed in injection techniques and their ability to inject subcutaneously should be assessed to ensure the proper administration of STELARA ® [see Medication Guide and Instructions for Use].
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: page_footer
blocks.text: Reference ID: 3376979
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Patients should be instructed to inject the full amount of STELARA ® according to the directions provided in the Medication Guide and Instructions for Use. The needle cover on the prefilled syringe contains dry natural rubber (a derivative of latex), which may cause allergic reactions in individuals sensitive to latex.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Needles and syringes should be disposed of in a puncture-resistant container. Patients or caregivers should be instructed in the technique of proper syringe and needle disposal, and be advised not to reuse these items.

blocks.text: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA ® ?
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA ® ?
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: STELARA ® is a medicine that affects your immune system. STELARA ® can increase your risk of having serious side effects, including:
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA ® ?
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Serious infections: STELARA ® may lower the ability of your immune system to fight infections and may increase your risk of infections. Some people have serious infections while taking STELARA ® , including tuberculosis (TB), and infections caused by bacteria, fungi, or viruses. Some people have to be hospitalized for treatment of their infection.
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA ® ?
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Your doctor should check you for TB before starting STELARA ® .
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA ® ?
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  If your doctor feels that you are at risk for TB, you may be treated with medicine for TB before you begin treatment with STELARA ® and during treatment with STELARA ® .
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA ® ?
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Your doctor should watch you closely for signs and symptoms of TB during treatment with STELARA ® .
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA ® ?
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: You should not start taking STELARA ® if you have any kind of infection unless your doctor says it is okay.
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA ® ?
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Before starting STELARA ® , tell your doctor if you think you have an infection or
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA ® ?
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: have symptoms of an infection such as:
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA ® ?
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  fever, sweats, or chills
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA ® ?
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  muscle aches
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA ® ?
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  cough
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA ® ?
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  shortness of breath
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA ® ?
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  blood in your phlegm
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA ® ?
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  weight loss
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA ® ?
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  warm, red, or painful skin or sores on your body
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA ® ?
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  diarrhea or stomach pain
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA ® ?
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  burning when you urinate or urinate more often than normal
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA ® ?
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  feel very tired
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA ® ?
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  are being treated for an infection
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA ® ?
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  get a lot of infections or have infections that keep coming back
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA ® ?
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  have TB, or have been in close contact with someone who has TB.
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA ® ?
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: After starting STELARA ® , call your doctor right away if you have any symptoms of an infection (see above).
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA ® ?
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: STELARA ® can make you more likely to get infections or make an infection that you have worse.
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA ® ?
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: People who have a genetic problem where the body does not make any of the proteins interleukin 12 (IL-12) and interleukin 23 (IL-23) are at a higher risk for certain serious infections. These infections can spread throughout the body and
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA ® ?
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: page_footer
blocks.text: Reference ID: 3376979
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: cause death. It is not known if people who take STELARA ® will get any of these infections, because of the effects of STELARA ® on these proteins in your body.
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA ® ?
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Cancers:
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: STELARA ® may decrease the activity of your immune system and increase your risk for certain types of cancers. Tell your doctor if you have ever had any type of cancer. Some people who are receiving STELARA ® and have risk factors for skin cancer have developed certain types of skin cancers. During your treatment with STELARA ® , tell your doctor if you develop any new skin growths.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Reversible Posterior Leukoencephalopathy Syndrome (RPLS):
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: RPLS is a rare condition that affects the brain and can cause death. The cause of RPLS is not known. If RPLS is found early and treated, most people recover. Tell your doctor right away if you have any new or worsening medical problems including:
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  headache
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  seizures
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  confusion
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  vision problems
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: What is STELARA ® ?
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: STELARA ® is a prescription medicine used to treat adults 18 years and older with:
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  moderate or severe psoriasis that involves large areas or many areas of their body, who may benefit from taking injections or pills (systemic therapy) or phototherapy (treatment using ultraviolet light alone or with pills).
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  active psoriatic arthritis. STELARA ® can be used alone or with methotrexate.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: STELARA ® may improve your psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis but may also lower the ability of your immune system to fight infections. This may also increase your risk for certain types of cancer.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: It is not known if STELARA ® is safe and effective in children.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Who should not take STELARA ® ?
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Do not take STELARA ® if you are allergic to ustekinumab or any of the ingredients in STELARA ® . See the end of this Medication Guide for a complete list of ingredients in STELARA ® .
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: What should I tell my doctor before receiving STELARA ® ?
section_path: What should I tell my doctor before receiving STELARA ® ?
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Before you receive STELARA ®
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: , tell your doctor if you:
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  have any of the conditions or symptoms listed in the section "What is the most important information I should know about STELARA ® ?"
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  ever had an allergic reaction to STELARA ® . Ask your doctor if you are not sure.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  are allergic to latex. The needle cover on the prefilled syringe contains latex.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  have recently received or are scheduled to receive an immunization (vaccine). People who take STELARA ® should not receive live vaccines. Tell your doctor if anyone in your house needs a vaccine. The viruses used in some types of vaccines can spread to people with a weakened immune system, and can cause
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: page_footer
blocks.text: Reference ID: 3376979
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: serious problems. You should not receive the BCG vaccine during the one year before taking STELARA ® or one year after you stop taking STELARA ® .
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  have any new or changing lesions within psoriasis areas or on normal skin.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  are receiving or have received allergy shots, especially for serious allergic reactions. Allergy shots may not work as well for you during treatment with STELARA ® . STELARA ® may also increase your risk of having an allergic reaction to an allergy shot.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  receive or have received phototherapy for your psoriasis.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  have any other medical conditions.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. It is not known if STELARA ® will harm your unborn baby. You and your doctor should decide if you will take STELARA ® .
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  are breast-feeding or plan to breast-feed. It is thought that STELARA ® passes into your breast milk. You should not breast-feed while taking STELARA ® without first talking with your doctor.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Tell your doctor about all the medicines you take, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal supplements. Know the medicines you take. Keep a list of them to show your doctor and
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: pharmacist when you get a new medicine.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: How should I use STELARA ® ?
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Use STELARA ® exactly as prescribed by your doctor.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  If your doctor decides that you or a caregiver may give your injections of STELARA ® at home, you should receive training on the right way to prepare and inject STELARA ® . Do not try to inject STELARA ® yourself until you or your caregiver have been shown how to inject STELARA ® by your doctor or nurse.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  STELARA ® is given by injection under the skin (subcutaneous injection), in your upper arms, buttocks, upper legs (thighs) or stomach area (abdomen).
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Do not give an injection in an area of the skin that is tender, bruised, red or hard.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Use a different injection site each time you use STELARA ® .
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  If you inject more STELARA ® than prescribed, call your doctor right away.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Be sure to keep all of your scheduled follow-up appointments.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Read the detailed Instructions for Use at the end of this Medication Guide for instructions about how to prepare and inject a dose of STELARA ® , and how to properly throw away (dispose of) used needles and syringes.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: What should I avoid while using STELARA ® ?
section_path: What should I avoid while using STELARA ® ?
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: You should not receive a live vaccine while taking STELARA ® . See "What should I tell my doctor before receiving STELARA ® ?"
section_path: What should I avoid while using STELARA ® ?

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: How do I store STELARA ® ?
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Store STELARA ® in a refrigerator, between 36ºF to 46ºF (2ºC to 8ºC) in the original carton until it is used.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Store STELARA ® vials upright.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Protect from light.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Do not freeze STELARA ® .
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Do not shake STELARA ® .
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Throw away (dispose of) any unused STELARA ® .
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Keep STELARA ® and all medicines out of the reach of children.

Do not give STELARA ® to other people, even if they have the same symptoms that you have. It may harm them. If you would like more information, talk with your doctor. section_path: Instructions for injecting STELARA ® using a prefilled syringe.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Read this Instructions for Use before you start using STELARA ® . Your doctor or nurse should show you how to prepare and give your injection of STELARA ® the right way.
section_path: Instructions for injecting STELARA ® using a prefilled syringe.

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: If you cannot give yourself the injection:
section_path: Instructions for injecting STELARA ® using a prefilled syringe.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  ask your doctor or nurse to help you, or
section_path: Instructions for injecting STELARA ® using a prefilled syringe.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  ask someone who has been trained by a doctor or nurse to give your injections.
section_path: Instructions for injecting STELARA ® using a prefilled syringe.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Do not try to inject STELARA ® yourself until you have been shown how to inject STELARA ® by your doctor, nurse or health professional.
section_path: Instructions for injecting STELARA ® using a prefilled syringe.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Important information:
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Before you start, check the carton to make sure that it is the right dose. You will have either 45mg or 90 mg as prescribed by your doctor.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: o If your dose is 45 mg, you will receive one 45 mg prefilled syringe.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: o If your dose is 90 mg, you will receive either one 90 mg prefilled syringe or two 45 mg prefilled syringes. If you receive two 45 mg prefilled syringes for a 90 mg dose, you will need to give yourself two injections, one right after the other.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Check the expiration date on the pre-filled syringe and carton. If the expiration date has passed, do not use it. If the expiration date has passed call your doctor or pharmacist, or call 1-800-JANSSEN (1-800-526-7736) for help.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Make sure the syringe is not damaged.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Check your prefilled syringe for any particles or discoloration. Your prefilled syringe should look clear and colorless to light yellow with few white particles.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Do not use if it is frozen, discolored, cloudy or has large particles. Get a new prefilled syringe.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Do not shake the prefilled syringe at any time. Shaking your prefilled syringe may damage your STELARA ® medicine. If your prefilled syringe has been shaken, do not use it. Get a new prefilled syringe.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  To reduce the risk of accidental needle sticks, each prefilled syringe has a needle guard that is automatically activated to cover the needle after you have given your injection. Do not pull back on the plunger at any time.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.text: Choose a wel l lit, clean, flat work surface.

blocks.text: Wash your hands well with soap and warm water.

blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Choose an injection site around your stomach area (abdomen), buttocks, upper legs (thighs). If a caregiver is giving you the injection, the outer area of t he upper arms may also be used. (See Figure C)

blocks.text: Do not give an injection in an area of t he skin that is tender, bruised, red or hard.

blocks.text: Clean the skin with an antiseptic wipe where you plan to give your injection.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not touch this area again before giving the injection. Let your skin dry before injecting.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not fan or blow on t he clean area.
